headline: Germany Ends Bundeswehr Use of Chinese-Made Commercial Drones
deck: The defence ministry says commercial models used for training and target work will be replaced over data and IT security concerns.
body: Germany’s defence ministry said the Bundeswehr will stop using commercially available Chinese-made drones for training and target work. [E1] [E6] Existing systems will be replaced by domestic or, where applicable, European products. [E2]
The ministry said the armed forces had used inexpensive, off-the-shelf drones for training, including target practice, and that units had bought them with minimal bureaucratic effort. [E4]

The ministry cited data and IT security as the reason Chinese-made models will no longer be used for that work. [E2] Its statement framed the change as strengthening the Bundeswehr’s self-sufficiency and technological sovereignty. [E5]
Der Spiegel first reported the decision amid worries that the drones could transmit data on military exercises, training grounds or weapons systems to Chinese intelligence services. [E3]
The restriction covers commercially available Chinese-made drones at military bases and training grounds, according to reports. [E6]
Der Spiegel reported that drones acquired by military units in recent years with limited bureaucratic oversight are being withdrawn from service as quickly as possible. [E7]
Local commanders had been allowed to buy drones under a 2024 strategy that included a white list of approved systems, including several made by China-based DJI. [E8]
Because there is no central record of purchases by individual units, the military has to impose a blanket ban, Der Spiegel reported. [E9]
